en: {count, plural, one {# message from you since this was asked (last {time})} other {# messages from you since this was asked (last {time})}}
ur: {count, plural, one {# پیغام آپ کی طرف سے، سوال کے بعد سے (آخری {time})} other {# پیغامات آپ کی طرف سے، سوال کے بعد سے (آخری {time})}}

context.note: The line under an OPEN ask in the terminal's ask list, stating how stale the question is: e.g. '3 messages from you since this was asked (last 19:36)'. {count} is an integer >= 1 (the caller draws no line at all for 0 or for an uncountable ask) and feeds the plural with `#`; {time} is an ALREADY-FORMATTED 24-hour local clock time (HH:MM) supplied by the caller — do not reformat, translate or wrap it in ICU date syntax. Both plural arms must be complete sentences because some languages reorder the parenthetical time; keep the parentheses and their wording inside each arm. This line is CLIPPED to the list's width with an ellipsis, so keep the opening words (the count and 'from you') first: the tail may be cut. The list paints one line per ask plus this line on stale open rows only, so the string must never contain a newline.

The second of two reasons the operator can give for closing an open ask, chosen with the arrow keys and Enter in the ask list's dismiss chooser. It means the operator already answered the question by typing in the conversation, so the agent should read their messages and treat the ask as settled (it is sent as reason=answered_in_chat). It is a reason, not a command: do not add a verb like 'send' or an exclamation mark. Keep it short — the label shares one painted row with its note. WIDTH, corrected after the first independent audit: the two reason controls and their cancel are a FLEX-WRAP row (the phone wraps them to separate lines rather than truncating), and the terminal draws the label and its note on ONE row clipped against the list's width — so 34 cells for a label and 44 for a note is the honest budget, and 'conversation'/'conversación'/'cuộc trò chuyện' fit it where a shorter synonym would have had to be invented.

context.note: The refusal shown in the all-conversations ask list when a dismissal finds the ask missing from THAT other conversation's log (a swept or reset store). The list's rows belong to other conversations by design, so this sentence must not claim the ask is absent from 'this session' — it is absent from the conversation the row named. It is a TOAST FRAGMENT like the queue's other refusals: lower-case opening, no trailing recovery clause (the row stays on screen and the key can be pressed again, so the surface already shows the way back).

context.note: The key-hint row at the foot of the ask list's dismiss chooser: Enter sends the highlighted reason, Esc goes back to the list without dismissing. Key names (enter, esc) are kept as the terminal spells them and joined with the middle dot separator the terminal's other hint rows use; keep that separator. Esc is named 'cancel' rather than 'back' because the key closes the chooser in place (elsewhere Esc collapses the whole surface), so one word must not name two exits. This row is dropped whole on a terminal too narrow for it, so it must stay one short line.

context.note: The one-line acknowledgement shown after the operator dismisses an open ask with the 'Answered in chat' reason. It reports what the queue recorded: the ask is gone and the agent was told the answer is already in the conversation. It must not read as 'your answer was sent' — nothing was sent, and that distinction is the whole point of the two reasons. WIDTH: 44 cells, the widest receipt any shipped locale needs (Spanish 42, Vietnamese 44); it is a whole line on its own, not a label.

context.note: The one-line acknowledgement shown after the operator dismisses a TIMED-OUT ask with the list's one-key control, which carries no reason. It must state the same fact the phone states for the same act (both surfaces read 'Dismissed — no reply sent' in English): the ask is gone and nothing was sent to the agent. It must NOT name 'no longer needed' or any other reason — the queue records its own default reason for this door, and that is a record, not a word the operator chose. Past tense, no exclamation mark.

The heading of the ask list's dismiss chooser: a line the operator reaches by pressing x on an OPEN ask, asking them to pick why the ask is going away. The code then joins the ask's own question after this heading with a middle dot separator (drawn by the code, not part of this value), so do not end the heading with punctuation or a separator. No exclamation mark; it names the act, it does not celebrate it.
